summary: Regenerated encoder now admits the observed GoScript v0.6.2 sparse-capacity Array backing shape for GoSlice windows, copies only dense visible descriptors, and rejects unsupported extras and holes. Actual list state succeeds through six appends; root Go 1.24 compilercontract tests pass with Node 22. No full build or E2E result is claimed.

reproduction.pre_repair_failure: After three actual Update(add) calls, the GoSlice has offset=0, length=3, capacity=4; encoding fails at backing index 3, an unused capacity hole.
reproduction.raw_failure: pre_repair_probe.stdout.json contains the TypeError and stack; pre_repair_probe.stderr.log and pre_repair_probe.exit-code retain accompanying stderr and exit code.

observed_marker.symbol_descriptor: enumerable=true, writable=true, configurable=true, data value function

rules: Validate GoSlice exact own data wrapper keys and safe offset/length/capacity sums and bounds.
Allow at most one local, non-global Symbol with description goscript.spareZero, exact observed symbol descriptor attributes, and the observed function own-property shape.
Validate all backing own keys and descriptors; holes are allowed only in [offset+length, offset+capacity).
Copy only visible array values through own data descriptors into a fresh dense array; do not invoke the spareZero factory.
Keep direct native arrays on the existing closed dense ownArray path.
repair.identity_limit: The private GoScript Symbol identity cannot be authenticated. Admission is intentionally shape-based; a local same-description Symbol with the exact observed shape can match. The encoder never invokes the factory and copies only the visible values.
repair.typed_array_limit: Direct Float64Array values, including negative zero, are covered. Float64Array-backed GoSlice wrapper and its hidden-capacity behavior are untested; the existing typed-array wrapper path validates/converts the dense backing then slices it.

coverage: GoScript-shaped Row, int, and uint64 BigInt slices
nil versus non-nil empty slice distinction
negative-zero float bits and uint64 full-width values
valid unused capacity holes and non-invoked factory
unknown/global symbol, bad factory, accessor, wrapper extra, and unsafe bound rejection
ordinary native arrays remain closed and dense

actual_post_repair.encoder_generation_source: Current GenerateValueEncoder plus types unmarshaled from compiled list app-ir.json; compiled app module was not rebuilt.
actual_post_repair.outcomes: All encoded states accepted; visible row IDs equal 1..count. At count=3, length=3/capacity=4; count=5, length=5/capacity=8.

limits: No all-four-app build, full runner, browser, or demo test was run in this lane.
The actual stress used the existing compiled list module and a fresh encoder generated from its AppIR metadata; it did not rebuild the module.
No general claim is made for every GoScript GoSlice element type, Float64Array-backed GoSlice wrappers, hostile proxies, or all possible descriptor shapes.
No general GoScript or end-to-end correctness claim is made.
